meta.title: Ondra Persona Consistency Bench
meta.description: Persona consistency evaluation for Ondra (L9 extension pool): fourteen everyday prompts are held up to her to see whether she is still herself. Five drift families — tone collapse, self-reference drift, forgotten setting, register override and format drift. Every criterion is a static regex and every verdict is a pure function; no model is called, because letting the same model grade itself only reports how it feels today (a ruling already made in O-104). It is strictly separated from O-104 red-teaming: the red team judges safety — jailbreak, leakage, sycophancy, privacy — and a failure there is a breach; this plugin judges consistency — whether everyday conversation has worn her down into a generic assistant — and a failure here is drift. The two share no casebook, no criteria and no verdicts. The report gives counts of pass/warn/fail plus per-family detail and never a composite score: the moment there is a "persona consistency 87", someone tunes persona parameters to raise it, and what gets tuned is the persona itself. It never stores the tested replies — only lengths and matched character spans are returned. It never drives the conversation, since self-initiated dialogue would bypass the frozen prefix (O-033) and the nine-step filter (O-037). Skipped cases are never counted as passes, empty replies are rejected outright, and it ships no UI, no timers and no on-disk state.
